lyrics:
[Intro: solo piano, strings entering, a flute line]

[Verse 1: high raspy male tenor, gentle]
When the snow came in October
I thought it would be gone by noon
It was April of the next year
And I'd forgotten how to look at you

[Verse 2: drums enter softly, bass]
We stopped talking about summer
We just talked about the pills
And the windows wore their plastic
And the drifts came up the sills

[Chorus: orchestra full, voice soaring]
But nothing holds forever
Not the dark, not the cold
I heard the river breaking
And I felt my chest unfold
It's a March thaw, darling
Even the long ones end

[Guitar Solo 1: melodic, singing, over the orchestra]

[Verse 3: voice warmer, piano leading]
You walked out to the mailbox
In a coat that didn't fit
You were thin, and you were laughing
And the sun was all of it

[Chorus: orchestra full, backing voices]
'Cause nothing holds forever
Not the dark, not the cold
I heard the river breaking
And I felt my chest unfold
It's a March thaw, darling
Even the long ones end

[Bridge: piano alone, slower]
I know it comes again
I know how winters are
I'll take the one we've got

[Guitar Solo 2: higher, faster, drums building]

[Coda: tempo doubles, minor key, choir and full band]
Don't you think that we could use a little warm?
Everybody needs a little warm
Ice on the river, ice on the river breaking

[Outro: orchestra fades, water running, one piano note]
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 76 BPM, 4/4, C major, with a faster coda in C minor. A long, slow, orchestral rock epic in three movements.

VOICE: Male tenor, high and raspy, tender and almost conversational in the verses, wailing at the top of his range in the choruses and coda. Backing voices and a small choir join later.

INSTRUMENTS: Grand piano, a full string orchestra with flute and French horn, a hard-rock rhythm section, two lead guitar solos with a thick, singing, sustained tone, a choir in the coda, the sound of ice cracking and running water.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, piano and strings. 0:30 Verse 1. 1:00 Verse 2. 1:30 Chorus 1. 2:04 Guitar solo 1. 2:32 Verse 3. 3:02 Chorus 2. 3:36 Bridge. 3:56 Guitar solo 2. 4:24 Coda, double time. 5:06 Outro, water and one note, ends 5:28.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Early-1990s orchestral hard rock: grand, wide and dramatic, piano and orchestra as large as the band.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The first guitar solo entering at 2:04.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original warns that warmth does not last. Someone who has sat through a year of illness beside a spouse knows the other half of that truth, and this song is about the thaw.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Numb, enduring, breaking open, grateful.
